NB2 §4 — Optimizers as steepest descent under a norm

Training Dynamics, Iliad Intensive 2026

To run the code, open td2_4_optimizer_geometry.ipynb in Jupyter (CPU only; needs numpy, matplotlib, scipy and torch). Every code cell's output is shown on this page; exercise solutions are folded under Solution.

To first order a step \Delta changes the loss by \langle g,\Delta\rangle, with g=\nabla L. That has no minimum until you bound the step’s size, and the norm you bound it in fixes the direction: \ell_2 gives gradient descent, \ell_\infty gives sign descent (Adam with its averages off), the Fisher norm gives natural gradient, and the spectral norm gives Muon’s orthogonalized update. Asking which norm lets step sizes transfer across width gives muP.

Update rules from SGD to AdamW, if you need them

\theta are the parameters, g the minibatch gradient, \eta the learning rate, \lambda the weight decay, \beta,\beta_1,\beta_2\in[0,1) EMA (exponential moving average) rates. Operations are per coordinate (g^2=g\odot g), t counts steps from 1, and m,v start at 0.

Optimizer Update Where it sits here
SGD \theta\leftarrow\theta-\eta g steepest descent in \ell_2, penalty form (§4.1)
Heavy ball m\leftarrow\beta m+g,\quad \theta\leftarrow\theta-\eta m same geometry as SGD; momentum filters the gradient sequence
RMSProp v\leftarrow\beta_2v+(1-\beta_2)g^2,\quad \theta\leftarrow\theta-\eta\,g/(\sqrt v+\epsilon) diagonal preconditioner; sign descent (\ell_\infty) at \beta_2=\epsilon=0
Adam m\leftarrow\beta_1m+(1-\beta_1)g,\ \ v\leftarrow\beta_2v+(1-\beta_2)g^2,\ \ \hat m=\dfrac{m}{1-\beta_1^t},\ \ \hat v=\dfrac{v}{1-\beta_2^t},\ \ \theta\leftarrow\theta-\eta\dfrac{\hat m}{\sqrt{\hat v}+\epsilon} smoothed sign descent (§4.3)
Adam + L2 Adam with g\leftarrow g+\lambda\theta the decay is divided by \sqrt{\hat v} too
AdamW \theta\leftarrow\theta-\eta\big(\hat m/(\sqrt{\hat v}+\epsilon)+\lambda\theta\big) decay outside the preconditioner; an implicit box \lvert\theta_i\rvert\lesssim1/\lambda (Exercise 4.3.E)

Momentum filters the gradient sequence (its stability is in NB2 §1); the norm then decides what step a filtered gradient becomes: Adam normalizes its momentum per coordinate, Muon orthogonalizes it. Adam’s bias correction undoes the zero start of m and v (Kingma and Ba 2015); defaults are \beta_1=0.9, \beta_2=0.999, \epsilon=10^{-8}. AdamW (Loshchilov and Hutter 2019) decouples the decay so that weights with a large gradient history are still shrunk; its role through normalization layers is NB2 §5.
